thread:
Oncall Bot: INCIDENT: Elevated 5xx and gateway timeouts detected for /v1/generate. Paging oncall. Severity: P1. Alerts: 504/502 spike, increased latency > 2s, batcher queue depth increasing rapidly. https://monitoring.example.com/d/abc123
Alex H: Acked. jumping in. seeing a spike in 504s from the ingress gateway as well.
Maria G: Confirming — N. Virginia region showing 5xx wave starting ~45s ago. Batcher queue depth metric 'scheduler.pending_requests' jumped from ~300 -> 1800.
SRE Lead: Oncall take? Who's primary?
Josh P: I'm primary. on my way. Initial hypothesis: head-of-line blocking in batching scheduler causing front-end timeouts (gateway gives up).
Support Bot: Notifying affected customers: cust-enterprise-phi and cust-saas-ops reported failed requests. Support ticket IDs: #4521, #4522. Customers see 504s and retries times out.
Alex H: Can someone grab recent gateway logs and the scheduler queue dump?
Josh P: pulling logs: `kubectl -n inference logs deploy/gateway -c gateway --tail=200`
Josh P: snippet: ```
[2026-03-15T18:44:12Z] 504 POST /v1/generate  in=2000ms out=502ms
[2026-03-15T18:44:13Z] 502 upstream read timeout: scheduler-unavailable
[2026-03-15T18:44:14Z] 504 request cancelled by client after 3s
```
Maria G: Scheduler metrics: `scheduler.active_batches` trending flat, `scheduler.pending_requests` ~1900, `batcher.max_batch_size` currently 1024, avg seq len short. We're packing many small requests into huge batches -> long wait for batch formation.
SRE Lead: That's head-of-line blocking. Options: reduce max_batch_size, lower batch_wait_ms, or bypass batching for small seqs (route to passthrough).
Alex H: While we triage, let's open a temporary pass-through route for high-latency requests. DevEx, can we flip a routing flag?
DevEx: I can toggle route policy. Which service id? use-route: generation-passthrough. Quick command: `curl -X POST https://console.redwood/api/route/toggle -d '{"route":"generation-passthrough","enabled":true}'`
Josh P: Doing rapid mitigation: 1) enable passthrough for latency-sensitive routes 2) set batcher.max_batch_size=256 3) reduce batch_wait_ms from 20ms -> 5ms. Applying now to v2 cluster.
Maria G: Applying config to scheduler canary (zone-a) first.
SRE Lead: Any idea on KV cache growth causing prefetch pressure? I saw some KV-prefetch errors earlier.
Josh P: KV-prefetch had a spike but not primary. Logs show `kv_prefetch_queue` spikes but eviction not severe. Main culprit is long tail waiting for full batch.
Alex H: Also customer-facing gateway is returning 502/504 due to backend timeouts. Short-term: increase gateway upstream timeout from 3s -> 8s to avoid premature cancellations while we adjust batching. This will reduce immediate 5xx but is not a fix.
DevEx: Gateway timeout bumped in region us-east-1. Command: `kubectl -n ingress set env deploy/gateway GATEWAY_UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT=8s`
Support Bot: Communicated to customers: "we're investigating elevated errors, mitigations in progress, ETA 30-60m".
Maria G: After reducing batch size and lowering wait, pending_requests dropped from 1900 -> 600 in ~90s. 5xx rate decreased by 70% in telemetry. Gateway 504s falling.
SRE Lead: Good. Keep an eye on cost — smaller batches increase per-token cost. This is acceptable for now.
Josh P: Noted. Leaving passthrough enabled for high-priority API keys only. Rollback plan: revert batching changes once queue stable <100 and 5xx < baseline for 15m.
Alex H: Any downstream customer impact on embeddings workers? We routed only /v1/generate. Embeddings unaffected.
Support Bot: Still seeing errors for cust-enterprise-phi but volume reduced. They report intermittent slow responses.
SRE Lead: Start postmortem template and assign owner. who's running follow-up?
Alex H: I'll own the follow-up for root cause. Josh — write action items for scheduler tuning and automation to detect rising pending_requests and auto-adapt batch size.
Josh P: On it. Action items: 1) autoscale batcher policy when pending_requests>500 for >30s; 2) implement dynamic batch size based on seq length distribution; 3) add alert for head-of-line pattern (many small seqs blocking large batch formation).
DevEx: I'll add a dashboard panel for small-vs-large seq distribution and add runbook steps for temporary passthrough toggles.
Maria G: Recommend follow-up run: KV-prefetch tuning in case future workload mixes cause cache pressure.
SRE Lead: Any blockers to handoff? Time is 02:12 UTC. We need coverage for the night.
Alex H: Handoff to Sam T for overnight watch. Sam — I've documented changes: reduced batch_size -> 256, batch_wait_ms=5, passthrough enabled for 'priority' API keys, gateway timeout bumped to 8s.
Sam T: Ack. I'll monitor and escalate if we see a re-increase.
Support Bot: Adding timeline to the ticket and notifying customers of mitigation update.
Josh P: Closing live mitigation: error rates down to ~10% of peak, pending_requests ~80, gateway timeouts back to nominal. Leaving temporary configs for now; rollback window TBD.
Alex H: We'll continue postmortem. Please add any logs, graphs to the incident doc. Incident declared: mitigated at 02:18 UTC.
Sam T: Will pick up and ensure rollback criteria are met.
SRE Lead: Thanks team. Follow-up owner: Alex H. Postmortem due EOD tomorrow.
DevEx: Runbook updates created: https://confluence.redwood/internal/incidents/runbooks/batcher-hol
Support Bot: Customers updated at 02:25 UTC with mitigations and next steps.
Oncall Bot: Incident ticket ID INC-2026-0315-07 created and linked. Severity updated to P1 -> mitigated.
Alex H: Note for postmortem: consider automated early fallback to passthrough if batcher.pending_requests rises > 1000 in < 60s.
Maria G: Also add tests for mixed small/large seq traffic in our load harness.
Josh P: thanks all. switching to monitoring-only.
Sam T: Handoff complete.
Support Bot: Closing customer-facing update thread, will reopen if regression occurs."
